info.title: Didit Auth API
info.description:
Programmatic registration and authentication API for developers and AI agents. Register in 2 API calls -- no browser needed. The most agent-friendly identity verification platform.

## Base URL

All endpoints in this spec are hosted at `https://apx.didit.me/auth/v2`. This is a different host than the verification API (`https://verification.didit.me/v3`). Keep them straight: this auth host issues your **JWT access tokens** and lets you list and manage your **organizations** and **applications**. The verification host is where you call sessions, workflows, AML, etc., authenticated with the **`api_key`** returned by this API.

## How the auth flow works

1. `POST /programmatic/register/` — submit email + password.
2. Receive a 6-character alphanumeric code by email.
3. `POST /programmatic/verify-email/` — submit the code. You get back a JWT `access_token`, a `refresh_token`, an organization, and a default application with `client_id` + `api_key`.
4. Save the `api_key`. Use it as `x-api-key` for every call to `https://verification.didit.me/v3/...`.
5. From any future machine, `POST /programmatic/login/` exchanges your email + password for a fresh JWT, then call `GET /organizations/me/` and the application endpoints to recover or rotate credentials.

The JWT is only needed for the **Account Management** endpoints in this spec; verification API traffic uses the long-lived `api_key`, not the JWT.

## Conventions

- All request and response bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).
- **Use a real, deliverable email address when testing `POST /programmatic/register/`.** The endpoint sends the verification code synchronously, so addresses on reserved test domains (`@example.com`, `@example.org`, `@*.test`, `@*.example`, `@*.invalid`) are refused by mail delivery and the request returns a `500`. Substitute the `you@yourdomain.com` placeholder in the samples with an inbox you can actually read.
- Validation errors return HTTP `400` with one of two envelopes: `{"field": ["message", ...]}` for field-level problems, or `{"detail": "message"}` for business-rule errors. A handful of validators (password strength on register, code expiry on verify-email) currently respond with a bare array `["message"]` instead of the field-keyed form -- this is a known server-side inconsistency, so client code should accept both shapes.
- Authentication errors come back as `{"detail": "..."}` with HTTP `401` (invalid bearer token) or `403` (missing bearer token / insufficient privileges).
- Rate-limit responses include a `wait` field with the cooldown in seconds.

tags.name: Programmatic Auth
tags.description: Email-and-password account lifecycle: register, verify, login. Returns the JWT `access_token` you use against the Account Management endpoints, plus (on verify) your first application's `client_id` and `api_key`.

tags.name: Account Management
tags.description: Authenticated endpoints (JWT bearer) that list organizations and create, fetch, or update applications. Use these to recover or rotate the `api_key` you authenticate verification API calls with.

post.description: Step 1 of programmatic onboarding. Creates a pending account and emails a 6-char code (10 min TTL). The address is checked before any account is created: one that cannot receive the code returns 400 `email_undeliverable`. Rate limits: 5/IP/hour, plus a shared hourly budget per network (/24 for IPv4, /64 for IPv6).

201.description: Registration successful. A 6-character alphanumeric verification code (e.g., `A3K9F2`) was emailed to the supplied address and is valid for 10 minutes. Call `POST /programmatic/verify-email/` next.

value.message: Registration successful. Check your email for the verification code.

400.description: Validation error. The intended envelope is `{"field": ["..."]}` for field-level errors and `{"detail": "..."}` for business-rule errors (e.g. duplicate email). Password-strength rules currently respond with a bare array `["..."]`, one rule at a time -- known server-side inconsistency; treat it as `{"password": ["..."]}` until fixed. When the address cannot receive the code (disposable, reserved or test domain, no mail server, a likely typo, or a previously bounced address), the body is `EmailUndeliverableError` with `code: "email_undeliverable"`; no account is created or changed.

password: Ensure this field has at least 8 characters.

value: Password must contain at least one uppercase letter.
Password must contain at least one lowercase letter.
Password must contain at least one digit.
Password must contain at least one special character (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?).

value.detail: An account with this email already exists.
This email can't receive messages. Please use a different email address.
This email can't receive messages. Please use a different email address.

429.description: Rate limited. More than 5 registration attempts from the same IP in the last hour, or the hourly budget for the caller's network (/24 for IPv4, /64 for IPv6, shared by registration and code resends) is used up. Both carry `Retry-After: 3600`. Also returned, with a `Retry-After: 5` header, when the service is momentarily checking as many passwords or codes as it can at once; retry after the indicated number of seconds.

value.detail: Too many registration attempts. Please try again later.

PasswordChecksBusy.summary: Too many password checks in progress

value.detail: Too many sign-in attempts are being processed right now. Please try again in a few seconds.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
Python
x-codeSamples.source:
from didit import Didit

# This call needs no API key.
client = Didit()

result = client.account.register(
    email="you@yourdomain.com",
    password="MyStr0ng!Pass",
)
print(result)

<?php

require 'vendor/autoload.php';

// This call needs no API key.

]);
print_r($result->toArray());

)
puts result.to_h

200.description: Email verified. The response contains tokens for this auth API plus the brand-new application's `client_id` and `api_key`. Persist the `api_key` securely — it is the long-lived credential used by every verification API call.

400.description: Validation error. The intended envelope is `{"field": ["..."]}` for field-level problems and `{"detail": "..."}` for business-rule errors (e.g. user not found). post.description: Authenticate any verified email/password Didit account and receive an RS256 JWT pair (default lifetime 86400s). Console-created email/password accounts can use this endpoint; OAuth-only console accounts must set a password first.

200.description: Login successful. Returns a fresh JWT pair. Use the `access_token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` against `/organizations/me/...` to look up the `org_id`, `app_id`, and `api_key`.

400.description: Validation error. Field-level problems with the request body.

InvalidCredentials.summary: Email + password did not match (also returned when the account does not exist, to avoid user-enumeration)

value.detail: Invalid email or password.

NotVerified.summary: Account exists but email is not yet verified

value.detail: Please verify your email address before logging in.

SSORequired.summary: The account belongs to an organization that requires SSO

detail.message: Your organization 'Acme Corp' requires SSO login.

403.description: The account was recovered and must set up a new sign-in method before it can log in. A link to do that was emailed to the account's address.

RecoverySetupRequired.summary: Recovered account with no sign-in method yet

value.message: You recovered your account. Open the link we emailed you to set up a new sign-in method.

429.description: Account locked (too many recent failures on this email) or IP rate-limited (too many attempts from this address). Also returned, with a `Retry-After: 5` header, when the service is momentarily checking as many passwords or codes as it can at once; retry after the indicated number of seconds.

value.detail: Account temporarily locked due to too many failed login attempts. Please try again later.

IPRateLimited.summary: More than 20/min or 100/hour from this IP

value.detail: Too many login attempts from this IP address. Please wait before trying again.

value.detail: Too many sign-in attempts are being processed right now. Please try again in a few seconds.

post.description:
Resend the 6-character verification code for an unverified programmatic account. Requires the account's email and password so only the owner can trigger a new code (no console Basic Auth). A fresh code replaces the previous one and is valid for 10 minutes.

Rate limits: a per-email cooldown of 60 seconds between resends (HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`), and the same 5-per-IP-per-hour and per-network hourly budgets as registration.

message.description: Always `A new verification code has been sent to your email.`

email.description: The address the code was sent to, normalized: lowercased, with any `+tag` removed from the local part (`Dev+test@Example.com` becomes `dev@example.com`).

example.message: A new verification code has been sent to your email.

400.description: Invalid email/password, or the email is already verified.

value.detail: Invalid email or password.
This email address is already verified.

429.description: Cooldown active (60s between resends) or IP or network budget exhausted (5/IP/hour and an hourly per-network budget, both shared with registration). Also returned, with a `Retry-After: 5` header, when the service is momentarily checking as many passwords or codes as it can at once; retry after the indicated number of seconds.

value.detail: Please wait before requesting a new code.

PasswordChecksBusy.summary: Too many password checks in progress

value.detail: Too many sign-in attempts are being processed right now. Please try again in a few seconds.

BearerAuth.description: RS256-signed JWT `access_token` returned by `POST /programmatic/login/` or `POST /programmatic/verify-email/`. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Default lifetime is 86400 seconds (24h). This token is only valid against the Account Management endpoints on `apx.didit.me/auth/v2`. The verification API (`verification.didit.me/v3`) uses the long-lived `api_key` as `x-api-key` instead.

email.description: Any valid email address (personal, work, alias). Used as the unique account identifier.

password.description: Minimum 8 characters. Must contain at least one uppercase letter (`A-Z`), one lowercase letter (`a-z`), one digit (`0-9`), and one special character from `!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?`. Validation reports one failed rule at a time.

message.description: Human-readable confirmation that the verification code was sent.
message.example: Registration successful. Check your email for the verification code.

email.description: The email the verification code was sent to.

code.description: 6-character alphanumeric code from the verification email. Codes expire 10 minutes after the most recent code was sent.

access_token.description: RS256-signed JWT. Use as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for Account Management endpoints on `apx.didit.me/auth/v2`.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token paired with the access token.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the access token in seconds (default 86400).

access_token.description: RS256-signed JWT. Use as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for Account Management endpoints.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the access token in seconds (default 86400).

uuid.description: Use as `{org_id}` on the application endpoints.

contact_email.description: Primary contact email for the organization.

OrganizationSummary.description: Minimal organization shape returned inline by `POST /programmatic/verify-email/`.

ApplicationCredentialsSummary.description: Minimal application shape returned inline by `POST /programmatic/verify-email/`. Persist the `api_key` immediately.

api_key.description: Use this as `x-api-key` on every verification API call. New keys start with `sk_live_` (live application) or `sk_test_` (sandbox application), followed by 43 URL-safe characters (letters, digits, `-` and `_`). Keys created before this format have no prefix and keep working unchanged.

Application.description: Full application record. `uuid`, `client_id`, and `api_key` never change after creation.

uuid.description: Application UUID. Use as `{app_id}` in subsequent calls.

name.description: Application display name shown in the Didit console.

client_id.description: Public client identifier, safe to embed in OAuth-style flows.

api_key.description: Long-lived secret (also called `client_secret`). Use as the `x-api-key` header for every call to `https://verification.didit.me/v3/...` (sessions, workflows, AML, etc.). Treat as a credential; never expose client-side. New keys start with `sk_live_` (live application) or `sk_test_` (sandbox application), followed by 43 URL-safe characters (letters, digits, `-` and `_`). Keys created before this format have no prefix and keep working unchanged. For 72 hours after you recovered your account, list, retrieve and update return an empty string here instead of the key.

website_url.description: Website or app URL associated with this application.

redirect_uris.description: Allowed redirect URIs for OAuth-style and verification redirect flows.

terms_url.description: Terms of service URL shown in the verification flow.

privacy_url.description: Privacy policy URL shown in the verification flow.

description.description: Internal description for the application (not shown to end users).

products.description: The application's products. Always all three, in this order: `identity`, `transactions`, `authentication`. A new application has `identity` enabled with every module on, and `transactions` and `authentication` disabled. Read-only: a `products` key in a create or update body is ignored.

ApplicationCreateRequest.description: All fields are optional. Sending an empty body creates an application with a default name.

name.description: Application display name. Defaults to `"<organization name> App"`.

website_url.description: Website or app URL associated with this application.

redirect_uris.description: Allowed redirect URIs for OAuth-style and verification redirect flows.

terms_url.description: Terms of service URL shown in the verification flow.

privacy_url.description: Privacy policy URL shown in the verification flow.

description.description: Internal description for the application (not shown to end users).

ApplicationUpdateRequest.description: PATCH body for application metadata. Send only the fields you want to change; omitted fields are preserved. `uuid`, `client_id`, and `api_key` cannot be updated. `products` is read-only: a `products` key in the body is ignored.

website_url.description: Website or app URL associated with this application.

redirect_uris.description: Allowed redirect URIs for OAuth-style and verification redirect flows.

terms_url.description: Terms of service URL shown in the verification flow.

privacy_url.description: Privacy policy URL shown in the verification flow.

ValidationError.description: Validation error body. The intended envelope is a `{field: ["message", ...]}` map for field-level errors or a `{detail: "..."}` single-key envelope for business-rule errors. A handful of validators (password strength on register, code validity on verify-email) currently respond with a bare array `["message"]` -- known server-side inconsistency. The schema below keeps that bare-array branch so client code generated from this spec deserializes today's responses, but new client code should treat it as the relevant field-keyed form (`{password: [...]}` or `{code: [...]}`) and the server contract will converge on that shape.

example.detail: An account with this email already exists.

RateLimitError.description: Rate-limit or progressive-lockout response. `wait` is the cooldown in seconds.

detail.example: Too many login attempts from this IP address. Please wait before trying again.

next.description: URL of the next page, or `null` on the last page.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or `null` on the first page.

next.description: URL of the next page, or `null` on the last page.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or `null` on the first page.

ApplicationProduct.description: One product of an application and its state. Read-only: the application endpoints return it and ignore it in a request body.

status.description: Whether the product is on for this application. `early_access` applies only to `authentication`, which Didit turns on for you.

modules.description: Module switches of the product, each `true` or `false`. `identity` has `user_verification`, `business_verification` and `case_management`. `transactions` has `travel_rule` and `case_management`. `authentication` has none (`{}`). `case_management` is one setting shown under both `identity` and `transactions`, so it has the same value on both.

EmailUndeliverableError.description: Returned by `POST /programmatic/register/` when the address cannot receive the verification code. The check runs before any account is created or changed, so nothing is left behind.

detail.example: This email can't receive messages. Please use a different email address.

reason.description: Why the address was refused: `invalid_address` (not a valid address), `reserved_domain` (a reserved or test domain such as `example.com`), `no_mail_records` (the domain has no mail server), `disposable_domain` (a throwaway mailbox provider), `possible_typo` (a likely misspelling of a common provider; see `suggestion`), `suppressed` (the address previously bounced or complained).

suggestion.description: The likely intended domain, present only when the domain looks like a typo (for example `gmail.com` for `gmial.com`). The API does not accept a confirmation: register again with the corrected address.

RecoveryHoldError.description: Returned for 72 hours after the account was recovered (lost sign-in methods were reset). Actions that create organizations, applications or secrets are refused until `until`; read operations keep working.

detail.example: This action is on hold because you recovered your account.

until.description: When the hold ends (ISO 8601). Retry the request after this time.

RecoverySetupRequiredError.description: The account was recovered and has no sign-in method set up yet. No tokens are issued; a one-time link to set up a new method was emailed to the account's address. Open it, set up the method, then log in again.

message.example: You recovered your account. Open the link we emailed you to set up a new sign-in method.
